summary: Factor g's lower and upper parts out: y(c) = (1 − u)g(1 − r(c)) with r(c) the part of X strictly below the diagonal for the order c within the sign blocks and u = r(−l). Flensted-Jensen's shift invariance gives ψ_l(g) = FJ_l(1, y(l)); triangularity gives Δ_q(y(l)) = Δ_q(g) for upper sets q of l (step 8). The theorem is about a lower set p (lowest entries of l): step 8 is applied to its complement ¬p (an upper set, step 20) and to the full index set (det y(l) = det g, step 21). Three applications of the compression lemma (for 1 − P on g − 1, for 1 − P on y(l) − 1, and for Q = kPkᴴ against P on y(l) − 1), compared through these, give the expansion of Δ_p(kᴴy(l)k); the error terms are bounded by norm arithmetic. (intro_lines 49–53 are not proof: they are the statement, lines 49–53 by the statement-boundary overlay of a second-reader message; the line census takes the `:=` of `let X :=` for the start of the value.)
